comment: Camera policy for the S10+ (beyond2lte). Read by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-camera-diag.sh. Sensors, V4L2/media nodes and firmware blobs are ENUMERATED and reported truthfully; a driver name in sysfs is NOT proof that a frame can be captured, and no frame is ever claimed without a real capture. There is NO Android camera HAL here and none is installed: the userspace path is V4L2 -> PipeWire -> xdg-desktop-portal Camera -> nuxel-home camera UI. Nothing in this file touches a partition, a block device or a bootloader.

front.name: s5k3j1
front.note: 10 MP front ISOCELL 3J1 (f/2.2) — observed on beyond2lte, corrects the historical s5k2l4sx guess

device.comment_expected: expected_on_s10plus is the SHIPPED HARDWARE, derived from the beyond2lte DTS and the S10+ specification. It is NOT an observation. What the running kernel actually binds is enumerated at runtime and is the only thing reported as present.

device_candidates.comment: All candidates are probed with shell globs; no /dev/videoN is hard-coded as truth. The first set that responds is reported with its real path.

firmware_blobs.comment: Vendor sensor/ISP firmware and calibration live under the vendor firmware paths. A blob being present is necessary but NOT sufficient: the sensor must also be bound and produce a frame. Missing blobs are reported as BLOCKED_FIRMWARE with the exact gap - never hidden, never substituted with a Pixel blob file.
firmware_blobs.never_install_comment: No Android camera HAL / framework library is installed or depended on (mission section 27).

pipeline.comment: The ready userspace chain. Each hop is reported independently so the FIRST failing stage is unambiguous.

stages.means: a sensor/bridge name is readable from the video4linux sysfs class
at least one expected firmware blob exists under a search path
a media device is present and readable (link/graph evidence)
a real frame is captured on an explicit owner command (never automated)

userspace_chain: V4L2 capture node (this tool enumerates it)
PipeWire camera node (published by the camera portal)
camera-gallery app (pwa/nuxel-apps/camera-gallery) via getUserMedia -> the portal's node
shared gallery/storage path (pwa/nuxel-apps/photos) for browsing captures

portal.comment: PRIVATE Nuxel camera broker (org.nuxel.Camera). It must NEVER claim the standard org.freedesktop.portal.Camera name with incompatible methods (A52 fix). The standard portal Camera interface (AccessCamera/OpenPipeWireRemote/IsCameraPresent) is not implemented here; it would require xdg-desktop-portal + PipeWire + a real capture backend.

synthetic_when_no_hardware.proves: the PipeWire -> portal -> WebKitGTK getUserMedia chain is intact
synthetic_when_no_hardware.not_evidence_of: the S10+ camera; a synthetic node must never be reported as hardware
synthetic_when_no_hardware.reported_as: synthetic=true on every line that mentions it
synthetic_when_no_hardware.comment: Synthetic (videotestsrc) is now OPT-IN via --test-source/--synthetic. The device-visible default is honest NO_CAMERA when no capture device exists; a synthetic node is never silently substituted as a real camera.

portal.on_missing: report the missing hop and the install path; never fall back to a hard-coded /dev/videoN

privacy.comment: Mission section 27 recording privacy. Recording is always user-controlled; there is no stealth mode, no hidden microphone/camera bypass and no way to suppress the recording indicator.
privacy.microphone_for_video: used only when the microphone is granted and the app is recording video; the mic is never opened by this tool

gallery.comment: The app pair the owner actually uses in the manual proof. The tool VERIFIES these paths and their declared bridge verbs exist; it never opens the camera on its own.

capture_app.capture_path: getUserMedia -> canvas.toBlob -> bridge camera.capture (file-backed, no data-URL/localStorage database)

gallery_app.note: browsing gallery; owned by the core-apps build group, referenced here so the owner is sent to a real path

gallery.bridge_comment: The shared bridge (services/nuxel-bridge) already exposes CameraCapture/CameraListCaptures; this file only asserts the contract the app declares.

output.comment: Where a captured still would go. This tool writes ONLY on an explicit `capture --yes` and never overwrites an existing file silently.
output.comment_metadata: EXIF orientation is recorded by the capturing app; this diagnostic does not rewrite metadata.
